By 1944-45 every Allied bomber stream flies with an integrated electronic defensive system: chaff, jamming, dedicated jammer aircraft. Terman, recruited by his old PhD adviser Vannevar Bush, runs the lab after Stanford receives a comparatively token $50,000 in wartime research funding and he leaves in frustration.

By 1950 Stanford's electronics department is being called the MIT of the West.
